[00:00] Nina Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Tuesday afternoon, can you hear me all right?
[00:05] Liam O'Connor: Yep, loud and clear Nina, thanks.
[00:08] Jasmine Lee: All good here.

[00:15] Nina Patel: Quick agenda - pipeline review, deal prioritization, any blockers (security/compliance), and then action items. We have about 40 mins, so we'll move through.
[00:25] Liam O'Connor: Sounds great. We'll start with Deal A, big retail customer. Close target mid-July but spotty RFP timeline, they asked about private deployment options and SOC two evidence, right?
[00:35] Nina Patel: yep that's right - Deal A is the one where they're asking about VPC and KMS integration. We have Redwood Private available; SE can speak to the network requirements.
[00:42] Marcus Wells: For Deal A, from a technical perspective, we should run a quick lat/throughput benchmark. Their seq lengths are about 1k tokens average when doing chat summarization, maybe heavy on embeddings too. Im thinking a GPU-backed Dedicated profile with quantization could hit the latency SLOs and lower token cost.
[00:58] Markus Vogel: I can share the actual token histogram, it's approximate. Also security team wanted to see SOC two report, SSO/SAML config, and proof of audit logs.
[01:08] Nina Patel: Good - we'll share SOC 2 and audit doc links after the call. Marcus, can you scope a perf test with their token profile?
[01:15] Marcus Wells: Yep, I'll spin up tests against a tuned quantized variant - but note, the RBC (redwoood?) - sorry, Redwood Dedicated variant will have slight differences in throughput vs Hosted. We'll document the delta.
[01:28] Jasmine Lee: On credits, customer is sensitive to cost. What's the typical co-sell credit or referral arrangement?
[01:34] Nina Patel: We have a standard partner credit structure for co-sell - reference one-pager i'll send; typically there's a % referral credit for pipeline influenced deals and optional joint discounts for committed capacity. We'll include examples.
[01:44] Liam O'Connor: Cool, that will help with pricing conversations. Deal A is the highest priority since they've got budget lined up but need the security checklist.
[01:52] Nina Patel: Noted. Moving to Deal B, enterprise analytics provider - longer sales cycle, but higher ACV. Equator has an intro to the customer's CTO; they asked about private on-prem and air-gapped options.
[02:05] Markus Vogel: They run in-prem infra, and their legal is strict. For air-gapped or air gap install, we have an on-prem package - but it requires a more detailed SOW and validation. It's higher lift.
[02:16] Marcus Wells: Tech caveat: on-prem installs mean we can't do continuous automatic updates; patch cadence will be contractual. We'll need network topology and support windows.
[02:24] Jasmine Lee: Should we aim a pilot first (POC scoping) for Deal B? Maybe 6-week POC.
[02:29] Nina Patel: Yes SE-led POC scoping sounds right, propose we book that early July. Marcus, can you lead the POC scoping with Markus and their engineers?
[02:36] Marcus Wells: Absolutely. I'll propose a scoping doc and checklist.
[02:40] Liam O'Connor: Timeline wise - customer wants exec sponsor intro this month if possible. I can make the intro once we have the SOW outline.
[02:47] Nina Patel: Great. Next, Deal C - smaller SaaS customer, short pilot window, cares about latency and token cost; they suspect OpenAI is cheaper but latency sometimes variable.
[02:58] Marcus Wells: For Deal C we can propose Redwood Hosted with caching and batching to reduce per-token cost while staying within latency SLOs. Show them the per-route dashboards in console. We should demo cost/latency tradeoffs.
[03:10] Jasmine Lee: What's the messaging we give when competitor (OpenAI/AWS) is cheaper?
[03:14] Nina Patel: Emphasize predictable SLAs, routing options, and the optimized runtime for production workloads - plus co-sell support and joint go-to-market. We'll also show the Optimize recommendations to lower cost.
[03:24] Liam O'Connor: Good. A few security questions from their InfoSec: encryption in transit + at rest, KMS, and audit logs.
[03:31] Nina Patel: We have KMS integrations and audit logs in Private and Dedicated; Hosted has configurable retention and encryption options - we'll share the security pack and SOC 2.
[03:39] Markus Vogel: For the benchmarks Marcus will run, include 95th pct latency and tail lat for streaming responses. Many customers care about tail behavior.
[03:48] Marcus Wells: Will do - I'll capture p95, p99, token cost estimates and config settings (batching, KV cache size, quant).
[03:56] Nina Patel: On enablement - Equator asked for a joint deck and a few one-pagers for sales. We have a partner co-sell deck; I'll tailor it with your logo and send a draft.
[04:05] Jasmine Lee: thanks, that'll help our reps. Also can we get a joint battlecard addressing common objections (latency vs cost, security)?
[04:12] Nina Patel: Yes, we'll include a battlecard.
[04:16] Liam O'Connor: Quick question on attribution: how do we track pipeline influenced by Equator?
[04:21] Tara Singh: We use the partner pipeline spreadsheet and tagging in CRM; also referral codes and partner tags in created deals. Nina will share the mechanics.
[04:29] Nina Patel: I'll send the exact tagging flow and sample CRM entries.
[04:34] [small cross-talk] Marcus Wells: sorry - there's a little background noise -
[04:38] Liam O'Connor: no worries.
[04:40] Nina Patel: Any blockers we should be aware of?
[04:43] Jasmine Lee: Just the security docs for Deal A and the need for a quick benchmark. Also a tighter pricing example for team to use in procurement conversations.
[04:51] Marcus Wells: On the benchmark - I might need a test account or sample payloads from Markus.
[04:55] Markus Vogel: I'll send the token histogram and sample payloads after the call, plus their network diagram.
[05:01] Nina Patel: perfect.
[05:04] [pause]
[05:10] Marcus Wells: For Deal B on-prem, one more note - if they want deterministic latency we recommend Dedicated in a co-located facility; otherwise on-prem installs can vary.
[05:20] Jasmine Lee: do we have pricing ranges for Dedicated vs Hosted to share?
[05:24] Nina Patel: we'll include sample tiered pricing in the one-pager. Also note committed reserved capacity reduces unit cost significantly.
[05:32] Liam O'Connor: Great. For next steps I'd propose: Redwood shares docs (SOC2, co-sell one-pager), Marcus runs benchmarks, Equator shares pipeline spreadsheet and network/security details, and we schedule a POC scoping meeting next week.
[05:46] Nina Patel: Agreed. Any other items?
[05:51] Jasmine Lee: can we get a short demo video clip or recorded console walk-through? Helps our reps.
[05:56] Marcus Wells: I'll record a 10-min console walkthrough showing per-route dashboards and routing policies.
[06:02] Nina Patel: Awesome, Marcus to share recording.
[06:06] [wrap up]
[06:08] Nina Patel: Ok thanks all - I'll send the follow-ups and draft co-sell deck. Marcus will kick off the benchmarks and scoping doc. Equator to share documents. We'll reconvene in 2 weeks or as needed.
[06:20] Liam O'Connor: Thanks everyone.
[06:22] Jasmine Lee: Thanks, bye.
[06:24] Markus Vogel: bye.
